type: new structural candidate; exact finite deterministic scheduling screen, not state-estimator Monte Carlo
motivation: Old single-link ACK theorem is frozen. Test shared-channel conflicts when per-link locally minimal attempt counts have different history-expiry deadlines.

model.tasks: One pending packet per link; all available at slot 0, common deadline n-1; stop a task after its first success.
model.channel: One attempted DATA packet per slot; trusted scheduler sees all relevant per-link failure histories and immediate authenticated ACKs.
model.attack: Separate effective-failure budget B_i in every physical sliding window L_i; adversary sees actual attempts causally. No FDI and no shared/global jammer budget.
model.horizon: n <= min_i L_i; all future failures remain inside the current window before the deadline.
model.resource_warning: Coordination and globally visible ACK histories are added assumptions versus center-free neighbor filtering; ACK airtime is abstracted into one slot, not proven free in practice.

hypothesis: Choose an attempt count r_i for each task; its latest admissible force-success slot is d_i(r_i)=max{t<=n-1: U_i(t)+r_i>B_i}. Shared feasibility is ordinary common-release preemptive EDF workload feasibility for these selected options. Min sum r_i should equal direct adversarial game optimum.

exhaustive.histories: all length L-1 binary words of weight <= B_i, zero before the stored prefix

baselines: Direct minimax Bellman game over actual physical suffixes; ACK success/failure outcomes explicitly enumerated, independent of proposed reduction
Per-link minimal count frozen initially, with its own effective deadline
Dynamic effective-deadline-first, recompute each slot; best of all fixed tie priorities per known instance
checks: All exact finite game values must equal option-reduction values
Constructed schedule verified against all legal success/failure branches for named examples
Two-link expiry-collision example declared before output: L=3,B=(1,1), histories=(0,1),(0,1), n=3
stop: Any reduction/game mismatch invalidates theorem. If no separation from a strong simple online rule, retain only a possible characterization, not a new scheduling algorithm. Even if valid, EDF/ILP/DP are standard; require direct near-neighbor fulltext before novelty claim.
